newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Senate voted on Monday 18-2 to ratify the bicameral conference committee's final report on the 433.8-billion national budget for 1997 and sent it to President Fidel Ramos for immediate signing into law within two weeks. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Supreme Court on Monday declared the Manila Hotel as part of national patrimony as it awarded sale of the hotel to Manila Prince Hotel Corp owned by Manila Bulletin chairman Emilio Yap. (PHILIPPINE STAR,PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER,MALAYA)
- Health Secretary Carmencita Reodica on Monday said hospitals found dumping toxic wastes into the Pasig River will be closed. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- Philippine telephone companies led by Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co are set to file within the week their respective petitions for an increase in their existing basic telephone rates ranging from 35 to 48 percent. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- The National Food Authority bought between 100,000 and 120,000 tonnes of yellow corn from China. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Pilipino Telephone Corp and Globe Telecom lost a staggering 1.3 billion pesos from cloning and fraud last year. (MALAYA)

- The Supreme Court's decision voiding the sale of the historic Manila Hotel to a Malaysian consortium blights the supposed level playing field touted to investors by the government, analysts and businessmen said. (MANILA TIMES)
